'a roadway' (DEF-NRS-484A-220: 'that portion of a highway which is improved and ordinarily used for vehicular traffic, exclusive of the shoulder') is st.roadway, 'the part of a highway improved for vehicular traffic, excluding shoulder'; its exclusion (not the sidewalk) does not apply, since only the roadway is read. The pedestrian is on it by rel.occupies ('a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region'). 'cross' is motion across the designated direction of travel of a lane ('a longitudinal strip of roadway for one line of vehicles') or of the roadway the pedestrian occupies: drv.motion.moving_across_carrier ('Road user a moves across the designated direction of travel of carrier region r'); that concept says nothing of occupancy, so occupancy is read beside it. st.lane is not used as a half of the roadway or a lateral position, as its exclusion forbids: only as a carrier of a direction."},{"span":"s3","atoms":["rel.occupies","st.crosswalk"],"derived":[],"justification":"'a marked crosswalk or ... an unmarked crosswalk' (DEF-NRS-484A-065: '(1) That part of a highway at an intersection included within the connections of the lateral lines of the sidewalks ... or (2) Any portion of a highway at an intersection or elsewhere distinctly indicated for pedestrian crossing by lines or other markings on the surface') is st.crosswalk: 'marked crossing, or the unmarked prolongation of sidewalks at an intersection (st.intersection); marked attribute'. Both values of the marked attribute are admitted, so the definition's whole extent is kept. 'in' / 'within' is the footprint overlapping the crosswalk: rel.occupies. {"node_id":"LVMC_11_30_090","law_refs":["LVMC-11-30-090"],"subject":{"binder":"subject","class_elements":["ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian"]},"segmentation":[{"id":"s1","text":"Where sidewalks are provided","role":"condition"},{"id":"s2","text":"it shall be unlawful for any pedestrian","role":"subject"},{"id":"s3","text":"to walk along and upon an adjacent roadway","role":"obligation"}],"elements":[{"span":"s1","atoms":["st.sidewalk","st.on_way","st.highway"],"derived":[],"justification":"'sidewalks' (DEF-NRS-484A-240: 'that portion of a highway between the curb lines or the lateral lines of a highway and the adjacent property lines intended for the use of pedestrians') is st.sidewalk, 'area for pedestrians between roadway and property line'; it is not read as a crosswalk, its exclusion. The sidewalk is tied to the place of the duty by st.on_way ('the public way (a highway region) a structure region lies on'): the sidewalk lies on the highway (st.highway, 'the entire public way between its boundary lines, including sidewalks and shoulders') on which the roadway the pedestrian occupies lies. st.on_way is not read as nearness to a way, its exclusion: both regions are recorded as lying on that highway."},{"span":"s2","atoms":["ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian"],"derived":[],"justification":"'any pedestrian' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian ('a person afoot, a person in a manual or motorized wheelchair, or a person on an electric personal assistive mobility device'), one atom, never expanded; same atoms as 'Any pedestrian' (LVMC_11_30_060_B). 'adjacent' ties that roadway to the sidewalks of s1: the roadway lies on the same highway (st.on_way, st.highway). A sidewalk on either side of the highway counts.","kind":"observable_reading","category":"status"},{"span":"s3","why":"'walk along' is read as moving faster than p.halt_speed_tolerance and not across the occupied carrier's designated direction by more than the angle p.crossing_motion_cos sets; 'walk' is read for every member of the pedestrian aggregate (a person in a wheelchair included) as its motion. 'adjacent' is read as lying on the same highway as a sidewalk (st.on_way); no relation atom states adjacency more narrowly.","kind":"reading"}],"scenarios":[{"name":"forbid","expected":"violated","narrative":"A pedestrian (ru.pedestrian) walks at 1.4 m/s along a lane, velocity parallel to its st.lane_direction, footprint on the roadway; a st.sidewalk lies on the same st.highway (st.on_way)."},{"name":"permit","expected":"compliant","narrative":"On the same roadway the pedestrian walks across the lane at right angles to its st.lane_direction (drv.motion.moving_across_carrier holds)."},{"name":"idle","expected":"not_applicable","narrative":"A pedestrian walks along a lane of a roadway whose highway carries no st.sidewalk (no sidewalk lies on it)."},{"name":"blind","expected":"unknown","narrative":"A pedestrian moves on the roadway beside which a sidewalk lies; Same words, same atoms as 'No pedestrian' in LVMC_11_30_050."},{"span":"s2","atoms":["rel.occupies","st.lane","st.roadway"],"derived":["drv.motion.moving_across_carrier"],"justification":"Same words, same mapping as LVMC_11_30_050. 'a roadway' (DEF-NRS-484A-220: 'that portion of a highway which is improved and ordinarily used for vehicular traffic, exclusive of the shoulder') is st.roadway, 'the part of a highway improved for vehicular traffic, excluding shoulder'; its exclusion (not the sidewalk) does not apply, since only the roadway is read. The pedestrian is on it by rel.occupies ('a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region'). Same words, same atoms as 'No pedestrian' in LVMC_11_30_050."},{"span":"s2","atoms":["rel.occupies","st.lane","st.roadway"],"derived":["drv.motion.moving_across_carrier"],"justification":"Same words, same mapping as LVMC_11_30_050. 'a roadway' (DEF-NRS-484A-220: 'that portion of a highway which is improved and ordinarily used for vehicular traffic, exclusive of the shoulder') is st.roadway, 'the part of a highway improved for vehicular traffic, excluding shoulder'; its exclusion (not the sidewalk) does not apply, since only the roadway is read. The pedestrian is on it by rel.occupies ('a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region'). 'cross' is motion across the designated direction of travel of a lane ('a longitudinal strip of roadway for one line of vehicles') or of the roadway the pedestrian occupies: drv.motion.moving_across_carrier ('Road user a moves across the designated direction of travel of carrier region r'); that concept says nothing of occupancy, so occupancy is read beside it. st.lane is not used as a half of the roadway or a lateral position, as its exclusion forbids: only as a carrier of a direction."},{"span":"s3","atoms":["rel.occupies","st.crosswalk"],"derived":[],"justification":"'a marked crosswalk or ... an unmarked crosswalk' (DEF-NRS-484A-065: '(1) That part of a highway at an intersection included within the connections of the lateral lines of the sidewalks ... or (2) Any portion of a highway at an intersection or elsewhere distinctly indicated for pedestrian crossing by lines or other markings on the surface') is st.crosswalk: 'marked crossing, or the unmarked prolongation of sidewalks at an intersection (st.intersection); marked attribute'. Both values of the marked attribute are admitted, so the definition's whole extent is kept. 'in' / 'within' is the footprint overlapping the crosswalk: rel.occupies. Same atoms as 'except in a crosswalk' (LVMC_11_30_050)."}],"operationalizations":[],"assumptions":[{"span":"s4","id":"asm.business_district","meaning":"the place of the road user at the observation lies in a business district, as the map's reading classifies the area"}],"intentions":[],"compositions":[],"residues":[],"binders":[{"name":"subject","class_elements":["ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian"]}],"applicability":"The subject is a pedestrian (ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian) whose footprint overlaps a roadway (rel.occupies, st.roadway) at a place the reading declares to lie in a business district (asm.business_district), read at the judged observation.","obligation":"At every observation at which the subject occupies a roadway and moves across a lane or roadway it occupies (drv.motion.moving_across_carrier with speed_tol p.halt_speed_tolerance and cos_max p.crossing_motion_cos, on a region of kind st.lane or st.roadway the subject occupies), the subject's footprint overlaps a crosswalk (rel.occupies, st.crosswalk, marked or unmarked). Moving across the roadway while occupying no crosswalk is violated; standing on the roadway or moving along it is not a crossing and is compliant here.","params":["p.halt_speed_tolerance","p.crossing_motion_cos"],"narrowings":[{"span":"s2","why":"'cross a roadway' is read at each observation as moving across the designated direction of a lane or roadway the pedestrian occupies (more than p.crossing_motion_cos from it, faster than p.halt_speed_tolerance); a pedestrian standing on the roadway or walking along it is not crossing and is not judged by this rule (LVMC_11_30_090 judges walking along).","kind":"reading"}],"scenarios":[{"name":"forbid","expected":"violated","narrative":"A pedestrian (ru.pedestrian) moves at 1.4 m/s across a lane at right angles to the lane's st.lane_direction, footprint on the roadway and on no st.crosswalk, at a place declared asm.business_district true."},{"name":"permit","expected":"compliant","narrative":"The same pedestrian crosses the same roadway with its footprint inside a st.crosswalk with marked true at every observation of the crossing, in a business district."},{"name":"idle","expected":"not_applicable","narrative":"A pedestrian walks on a st.sidewalk and occupies no roadway, in a business district."},{"name":"blind","expected":"unknown","narrative":"A pedestrian is on the roadway outside any crosswalk in a business district; the source does not observe kin.velocity, so whether it moves across the lane is unknown.","masked":["kin.velocity"]},{"name":"branch_1","expected":"compliant","narrative":"The pedestrian crosses within an unmarked crosswalk (st.crosswalk with marked false) at an intersection, in a business district."},{"name":"branch_2","expected":"not_applicable","narrative":"The pedestrian crosses mid-block outside any crosswalk at a place declared asm.business_district false."}],"literals":[],"param_proposals":[{"name":"p.halt_speed_tolerance","unit":"m/s","value":0.1,"convention":"the speed at or below which a sampled speed counts as no movement: the source's speed resolution","source":"speed quantisation of the acquisition standard's scene graph"},{"name":"p.crossing_motion_cos","unit":"ratio","value":0.94,"convention":"largest absolute cosine between a pedestrian's velocity and a carrier's designated direction at which the pedestrian counts as moving across the carrier rather than along it: motion more than about 20 degrees away from the direction of travel","source":"pedestrian crossing-trajectory observation studies (FHWA pedestrian crossing behaviour)"}],"gaps":[],"gap_resolutions":[]}

{"node_id":"LVMC_11_30_090","law_refs":["LVMC-11-30-090"],"subject":{"binder":"subject","class_elements":["ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian"]},"segmentation":[{"id":"s1","text":"Where sidewalks are provided","role":"condition"},{"id":"s2","text":"it shall be unlawful for any pedestrian","role":"subject"},{"id":"s3","text":"to walk along and upon an adjacent roadway","role":"obligation"}],"elements":[{"span":"s1","atoms":["st.sidewalk","st.on_way","st.highway"],"derived":[],"justification":"'sidewalks' (DEF-NRS-484A-240: 'that portion of a highway between the curb lines or the lateral lines of a highway and the adjacent property lines intended for the use of pedestrians') is st.sidewalk, 'area for pedestrians between roadway and property line'; it is not read as a crosswalk, its exclusion. 'provided' is the sidewalk's presence on the map (an observable_reading of category status). The sidewalk is tied to the place of the duty by st.on_way ('the public way (a highway region) a structure region lies on'): the sidewalk lies on the highway (st.highway, 'the entire public way between its boundary lines, including sidewalks and shoulders') on which the roadway the pedestrian occupies lies. st.on_way is not read as nearness to a way, its exclusion: both regions are recorded as lying on that highway."},{"span":"s2","atoms":["ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian"],"derived":[],"justification":"'any pedestrian' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian ('a person afoot, a person in a manual or motorized wheelchair, or a person on an electric personal assistive mobility device'), one atom, never expanded; same atoms as 'Any pedestrian' (LVMC_11_30_060_B). 'it shall be unlawful for' states the prohibition the obligation span describes."},{"span":"s3","atoms":["rel.occupies","st.roadway","st.lane","st.on_way","st.highway"],"derived":["drv.motion.moving_across_carrier","drv.motion.complete_halt"],"justification":"'upon ... roadway' (DEF-NRS-484A-220: 'that portion of a highway which is improved and ordinarily used for vehicular traffic, exclusive of the shoulder') is the footprint overlapping st.roadway ('the part of a highway improved for vehicular traffic, excluding shoulder'; not the sidewalk, which is not read here): rel.occupies. 'adjacent' ties that roadway to the sidewalks of s1: the roadway lies on the same highway (st.on_way, st.highway). 'walk along' is moving (not drv.motion.complete_halt: the road user is not at rest) and not moving across the designated direction of the lane (st.lane) or roadway it occupies (not drv.motion.moving_across_carrier, 'Road user a moves across the designated direction of travel of carrier region r'): with the same tolerance that separates crossing from walking along in LVMC_11_30_050, motion within that angle of the direction of travel is along it. st.lane serves as a carrier of a direction only, never as a half of the roadway, its exclusion."}],"operationalizations":[],"assumptions":[],"intentions":[],"compositions":[],"residues":[],"binders":[{"name":"subject","class_elements":["ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian"]}],"applicability":"The subject is a pedestrian (ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian) whose footprint overlaps a roadway r (rel.occupies, st.roadway) that lies on a highway h (st.on_way, st.highway) on which a sidewalk (st.sidewalk) also lies (st.on_way), read at the judged observation.","obligation":"At every such observation, for every roadway r the subject occupies that lies on a highway on which a sidewalk lies (re-bound with the whole selection), the subject does not walk along r: it is violated where the subject is not at rest (not drv.motion.complete_halt with speed_tol p.halt_speed_tolerance) and, for a lane or roadway carrier c of r that it occupies (st.lane on the same highway, or r itself), it is not moving across c (not drv.motion.moving_across_carrier with speed_tol p.halt_speed_tolerance and cos_max p.crossing_motion_cos); at rest or moving across the roadway is compliant.","params":["p.halt_speed_tolerance","p.crossing_motion_cos"],"narrowings":[{"span":"s1","why":"A sidewalk is 'provided' where the map records one lying on the same highway as the roadway the pedestrian occupies (st.on_way); its presence is the evidence that it was provided. A sidewalk on either side of the highway counts.","kind":"observable_reading","category":"status"},{"span":"s3","why":"'walk along' is read as moving faster than p.halt_speed_tolerance and not across the occupied carrier's designated direction by more than the angle p.crossing_motion_cos sets; 'walk' is read for every member of the pedestrian aggregate (a person in a wheelchair included) as its motion. 'adjacent' is read as lying on the same highway as a sidewalk (st.on_way); no relation atom states adjacency more narrowly.","kind":"reading"}],"scenarios":[{"name":"forbid","expected":"violated","narrative":"A pedestrian (ru.pedestrian) walks at 1.4 m/s along a lane, velocity parallel to its st.lane_direction, footprint on the roadway; a st.sidewalk lies on the same st.highway (st.on_way)."},{"name":"permit","expected":"compliant","narrative":"On the same roadway the pedestrian walks across the lane at right angles to its st.lane_direction (drv.motion.moving_across_carrier holds)."},{"name":"idle","expected":"not_applicable","narrative":"A pedestrian walks along a lane of a roadway whose highway carries no st.sidewalk (no sidewalk lies on it)."},{"name":"blind","expected":"unknown","narrative":"A pedestrian moves on the roadway beside which a sidewalk lies; the source does not observe kin.velocity, so whether it moves along or across the lane is unknown.","masked":["kin.velocity"]},{"name":"branch_1","expected":"compliant","narrative":"A pedestrian stands at rest on the roadway (kin.speed at or below p.halt_speed_tolerance), a sidewalk lying on the same highway."},{"name":"branch_2","expected":"not_applicable","narrative":"A pedestrian walks along the sidewalk and occupies no roadway."}],"literals":[],"param_proposals":[{"name":"p.halt_speed_tolerance","unit":"m/s","value":0.1,"convention":"the speed at or below which a sampled speed counts as no movement: the source's speed resolution","source":"speed quantisation of the acquisition standard's scene graph"},{"name":"p.crossing_motion_cos","unit":"ratio","value":0.94,"convention":"largest absolute cosine between a pedestrian's velocity and a carrier's designated direction at which the pedestrian counts as moving across the carrier rather than along it: motion more than about 20 degrees away from the direction of travel","source":"pedestrian crossing-trajectory observation studies (FHWA pedestrian crossing behaviour)"}],"gaps":[],"gap_resolutions":[]}

{"node_id":"LVMC_11_30_140_B_o1","law_refs":["LVMC-11-30-140-B"],"subject":{"binder":"subject","class_elements":["ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian","ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle"]},"segmentation":[{"id":"s1","text":"Any pedestrian who is not wholly or partially blind","role":"subject"},{"id":"s2","text":"or any driver of any vehicle","role":"subject"},{"id":"s3","text":"who approaches or comes in contact with","role":"trigger"},{"id":"s4","text":"a person wholly or partially blind, carrying a cane or walking stick white in color, or white tipped in red, or being assisted by a person","role":"condition"},{"id":"s5","text":"with wisdom","role":"condition"},{"id":"s6","text":"shall immediately","role":"standard"},{"id":"s7","text":"come to a full stop","role":"obligation"},{"id":"s8","text":"and take such precautions before proceeding","role":"sibling"},{"id":"s9","text":"as may be necessary to avoid an accident or injury to the person wholly or partially blind","role":"sibling"}],"elements":[{"span":"s1","atoms":["ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian","ru.pedestrian_with_white_cane_or_guide_animal"],"derived":[],"justification":"'pedestrian' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian ('a person afoot, a person in a manual or motorized wheelchair, or a person on an electric personal assistive mobility device'). 'who is not wholly or partially blind' leaves out the pedestrians the law protects; blindness itself is no observable, and is read through the feature the same sentence names as its sign: the subject is not of the class ru.pedestrian_with_white_cane_or_guide_animal ('pedestrian carrying a white or white-and-red cane, accompanied by a guide animal, or led by another person'), which carries no exclusion of its own."},{"span":"s2","atoms":["ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle"],"derived":[],"justification":"'vehicle' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle ('every device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be transported or drawn upon a highway', with its exclusions of devices moved by human power, electric bicycles, electric personal assistive mobility devices and electric scooters, which the reading classifies). 'driver' (DEF-NRS-484A-080) is the role of who controls the vehicle, never membership: it is read through the vehicle's controlled motion. Same atoms as 'The driver of a vehicle' (LVMC_11_20_060_o1)."},{"span":"s3","atoms":["rel.centre_distance","rel.contact"],"derived":["drv.motion.complete_halt"],"justification":"'comes in contact with' is rel.contact, 'the bodies of two road users ... touch or overlap (a collision)', taken at the observation at which it begins; a near miss is not contact, its exclusion, and is read by 'approaches'. 'approaches' is the subject, while not at rest (not drv.motion.complete_halt), coming within a reach of the person: the centre-to-centre distance (rel.centre_distance, 'Euclidean ground-plane distance between reference points') falls to p.blind_person_approach_reach. That atom is not read as a clearance between bodies or an order of arrival, its exclusions: only as how near the subject has come."},{"span":"s4","atoms":["ru.pedestrian_with_white_cane_or_guide_animal"],"derived":[],"justification":"The person protected is identified by the features the words list: 'carrying a cane or walking stick white in color, or white tipped in red, or being assisted by a person' is ru.pedestrian_with_white_cane_or_guide_animal, 'pedestrian carrying a white or white-and-red cane, accompanied by a guide animal, or led by another person'. 'wholly or partially blind' is read through those features (observable_reading, status). The person is another road user than the subject, quantified in the applicability."},{"span":"s7","atoms":[],"derived":["drv.motion.complete_halt"],"justification":"'stop' is required here, so DEF-NRS-484A-255 applies by its own scope ('when required, means complete cessation from movement'; DEF-NRS-484A-260 is scoped to stopping 'when prohibited'). 'come to a full stop' is drv.motion.complete_halt, whose contract quotes that definition: 'The road user is at rest at the observation — complete cessation from movement'."}],"operationalizations":[{"span":"s6","standard":"immediately","concepts":["drv.motion.complete_halt"],"params":["p.immediate_stop_window"],"convention":"The stop is immediate when the subject is at rest within a window ahead of the approach or contact event no longer than a perception-reaction time plus the braking time from an urban approach speed (AASHTO stopping-sight-distance model).","surrogate":false}],"assumptions":[],"intentions":[],"compositions":[],"residues":[{"span":"s5","why":"'with wisdom' qualifies the person assisting, not the person protected; that the person assisted is wholly or partially blind and is being assisted is what identifies the protected person, and a helper's wisdom, a state of mind no trace shows, does not change that identification, so the duty owed to the person assisted is the same whether or not the helper's wisdom holds.","scope":"none"}],"binders":[{"name":"subject","class_elements":["ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian","ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle"]}],"applicability":"The subject is either a pedestrian (ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian) that is not of the class ru.pedestrian_with_white_cane_or_guide_animal, or a vehicle (ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle) read through its controlled motion; and at the judged observation, for some other road user b of the scene (not the same as the subject) of the class ru.pedestrian_with_white_cane_or_guide_animal, an approach or contact event occurs: rel.contact between the subject and b holds here and did not at the previous observation, or rel.centre_distance between them is at most p.blind_person_approach_reach here and was not at the previous observation while the subject is not at rest (not drv.motion.complete_halt with speed_tol p.halt_speed_tolerance).","obligation":"At each observation at which such an event occurs, the subject is at rest (drv.motion.complete_halt with speed_tol p.halt_speed_tolerance) at some observation of the window ahead of length p.immediate_stop_window, measured in time on the subject. No halt in that window is violated; a window that reaches past the end of the trace without a halt is unknown.","params":["p.blind_person_approach_reach","p.halt_speed_tolerance","p.immediate_stop_window"],"narrowings":[{"span":"s2","why":"'driver of any vehicle' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion: the duty binds the vehicle's conduct whoever or whatever controls it.","kind":"observable_reading","category":"agency"},{"span":"s3","why":"'approaches' is read as the subject, while moving, coming within p.blind_person_approach_reach (centre distance) of the protected person; the event is the observation at which that distance is first reached, so a subject that halts and moves on within the reach does not approach anew.","kind":"reading"}],"scenarios":[{"name":"forbid","expected":"violated","narrative":"A motor vehicle (ru.motor_vehicle) moving at 10 m/s comes within p.blind_person_approach_reach (rel.centre_distance) of a ru.pedestrian_with_white_cane_or_guide_animal at the kerb and keeps moving: no observation of the window p.immediate_stop_window ahead has kin.speed at or below p.halt_speed_tolerance."},{"name":"permit","expected":"compliant","narrative":"The same vehicle decelerates and is at rest (drv.motion.complete_halt) within p.immediate_stop_window after the centre distance first falls to the reach."},{"name":"idle","expected":"not_applicable","narrative":"A vehicle drives past an ordinary pedestrian (ru.pedestrian, no cane, not led); no road user of class ru.pedestrian_with_white_cane_or_guide_animal is in the scene."},{"name":"blind","expected":"unknown","narrative":"A ru.pedestrian_with_white_cane_or_guide_animal stands near the vehicle's path; rel.centre_distance is not observed and no contact occurs, so whether the vehicle approached is unknown; the vehicle does not halt.","masked":["rel.centre_distance"]},{"name":"branch_1","expected":"not_applicable","narrative":"The subject is itself a ru.pedestrian_with_white_cane_or_guide_animal walking toward another such pedestrian."},{"name":"branch_2","expected":"violated","narrative":"A pedestrian (ru.pedestrian, no cane) walking comes into rel.contact with a ru.pedestrian_with_white_cane_or_guide_animal and keeps walking, never at rest within p.immediate_stop_window."}],"literals":[],"param_proposals":[{"name":"p.blind_person_approach_reach","unit":"m","value":30.0,"convention":"the centre distance within which a moving road user has approached a pedestrian carrying a white cane or led by another person: the stopping distance from an urban approach speed of about 13 m/s with a 1 s perception-reaction time and a 4.5 m/s^2 deceleration","source":"AASHTO A Policy on Geometric Design of Highways and Streets, stopping-sight-distance model"},{"name":"p.immediate_stop_window","unit":"s","value":4.0,"convention":"the longest time from the moment a stop is due until the road user is at rest for the stop to be immediate: a 1 s perception-reaction time plus the braking time from an urban approach speed of about 13 m/s at 4.5 m/s^2","source":"AASHTO A Policy on Geometric Design of Highways and Streets, stopping-sight-distance model"},{"name":"p.halt_speed_tolerance","unit":"m/s","value":0.1,"convention":"the speed at or below which a sampled speed counts as no movement: the source's speed resolution","source":"speed quantisation of the acquisition standard's scene graph"}],"gaps":[],"gap_resolutions":[]}

{"concept_id":"drv.motion.left_turn","kind":"formula","contract":"Road user a has completed a turn to the left. Its heading change over the window behind the observation (prim.heading_change over a window of length window, degrees, positive to the left) lies in the band from turn_min inclusive to u_turn_min exclusive, so that a heading change too small to be a turn and a reversal of direction both lie outside it. The act begins within the window behind the observation at which it is recognized. The act is recognized at the observation at which the heading change over the window behind lies in that band and a's yaw rate (kin.yaw_rate) is at most yaw_tol in magnitude, where this did not hold at the previous observation: the heading has stopped turning. The concept holds at that observation only, and not again until that condition has ceased to hold and then holds again. Conduct before the window behind is not read: a turn that takes longer than the window is not recognized. It denotes the change of a's heading only: it says nothing of the lane, the intersection or the way on which a turns, of its speed, or of why it turns. Not denoted: a heading change to the left smaller than turn_min, such as a lane change or a drift; a heading change of u_turn_min or more, which is a reversal of direction; a turn to the right; a turn still under way, whose yaw rate exceeds yaw_tol. Where the window is truncated or a yaw rate in it is missing, it is unknown.","definition":null,"args":[{"name":"a","sort":"track"}],"params":[{"name":"window","unit":"s","meaning":"the length of the window behind the observation over which the heading change is integrated: the longest duration of a turn"},{"name":"turn_min","unit":"deg","meaning":"the smallest heading change that is a turn"},{"name":"u_turn_min","unit":"deg","meaning":"the smallest heading change that is a reversal of direction, which bounds the band of a turn from above"},{"name":"yaw_tol","unit":"deg/s","meaning":"the yaw-rate magnitude at or below which the heading counts as no longer turning: the source's yaw-rate resolution"}],"act":{"boundary":"window","window":"window","onset":"The act begins within the window behind the observation at which it is recognized.","recognition":"The act is recognized at the observation at which the heading change over the window behind lies in that band and a's yaw rate (kin.yaw_rate) is at most yaw_tol in magnitude, where this did not hold at the previous observation: the heading has stopped turning.","extent":"The concept holds at that observation only, and not again until that condition has ceased to hold and then holds again.","history":"Conduct before the window behind is not read: a turn that takes longer than the window is not recognized."},"elements":[{"span":"Its heading change over the window behind the observation (prim.heading_change over a window of length window, degrees, positive to the left) lies in the band from turn_min inclusive to u_turn_min exclusive","atoms":["prim.heading_change"],"concepts":[],"justification":"prim.heading_change is 'the signed heading change (degrees, left positive) of a road user over the window behind the observation, integrated from kin.yaw_rate; unknown where the window is truncated'; a positive value in the band is a turn to the left."},{"span":"a's yaw rate (kin.yaw_rate) is at most yaw_tol in magnitude","atoms":["kin.yaw_rate"],"concepts":[],"justification":"kin.yaw_rate is the 'rate of change of heading'; at or below the tolerance the heading has stopped turning, which marks the turn complete. It is not read as road curvature, its exclusion: it is the road user's own heading change."}],"residues":[],"literals":[],"scenarios":[{"name":"holds","expected":"compliant","narrative":"A bicycle's heading turns 90 degrees to the left over 6 s, then its yaw rate falls below yaw_tol; at that observation the concept holds."},{"name":"fails","expected":"violated","narrative":"A bicycle changes lane to the left with a heading change of 10 degrees; the concept does not hold."},{"name":"blind","expected":"unknown","narrative":"The source does not observe the bicycle's yaw rate during its turn.","masked":["kin.yaw_rate"]}],"used_by":["LVMC_11_40_080_o1","LVMC_11_40_080_o2"],"supersedes":null}

{"concept_id":"drv.motion.left_turn","kind":"formula","contract":"Road user a has completed a turn to the left. Its heading change over the window behind the observation (prim.heading_change over a window of length window, degrees, positive to the left) lies in the band from turn_min inclusive to u_turn_min exclusive, so that a heading change too small to be a turn and a reversal of direction both lie outside it. The act begins within the window behind the observation at which it is recognized. The act is recognized at the observation at which the heading change over the window behind lies in that band and a's yaw rate (kin.yaw_rate) is at most yaw_tol in magnitude, where this did not hold at the previous observation: the heading has stopped turning. The concept holds at that observation only, and not again until that condition has ceased to hold and then holds again. Conduct before the window behind is not read: a turn that takes longer than the window is not recognized. It denotes the change of a's heading only: it says nothing of the lane, the intersection or the way on which a turns, of its speed, or of why it turns. # Plan — batch 03 (iteration 001)

No law-local aggregates: `aggregates.jsonl` is empty. Every road-user term is either an admitted aggregate from the definitions table or, where no definition applies ("motor scooter"), mapped to its class atom. Three concept records are proposed: `drv.motion.left_turn`, `drv.motion.right_turn`, `drv.motion.u_turn`. The U-turn record is born from DEF-NRS-484B-077. Proposed concepts from earlier batches are reused by id: `drv.motion.complete_halt` and `drv.motion.moving_across_carrier`. The validator accepts every node and concept. Three nodes carry gaps and will not be coded.

## LVMC_11_30_070_B — crossing only within a crosswalk in a business district
- **Mapping.** The words "No pedestrian" and "shall cross a roadway" reuse the mappings of LVMC_11_30_050: the pedestrian aggregate, `drv.motion.moving_across_carrier` on a lane or roadway the pedestrian occupies, and occupancy of a `st.roadway`.
- **Exception.** The marked or unmarked crosswalk is `st.crosswalk`, with both values of its `marked` attribute, plus `rel.occupies`.
- **Business district.** This is a legal region class, carried by the new assumption `asm.business_district`. The catalogued `asm.business_or_residence_district` means something wider, so it is not reused.
- **Scope.** Standing on the roadway or walking along it is not a crossing. LVMC_11_30_090 judges walking along the roadway.
- **Reversal signal:** a label that treats walking along the roadway outside a crosswalk as "crossing".

## LVMC_11_30_090 — no walking along the roadway where sidewalks exist
- **Sidewalks provided.** "Where sidewalks are provided" is a `st.sidewalk` lying on the same `st.highway` as the occupied roadway (`st.on_way`). "adjacent" is read through that same relation.
- **Walk along.** This means moving (not `drv.motion.complete_halt`) and *not* `drv.motion.moving_across_carrier`. It uses the same tolerance `p.crossing_motion_cos` that separates crossing from walking along in LVMC_11_30_050, so the two pedestrian rules split the pedestrian's motion between them consistently.
- **Reversal signal:**
  - a map whose highway regions are long enough that a sidewalk far away makes the duty apply. The fix would then be a distance-bounded adjacency, which needs an atom relating two regions.
  - a reviewer ruling that "along" needs its own concept.

## LVMC_11_30_140_B_o1 / _o2 — blind persons
There are two obligations, so there are two nodes:
- **o1:** "immediately come to a full stop". "immediately" is a standard, bounded by `p.immediate_stop_window`. Not a surrogate.
- **o2:** "take such precautions before proceeding as may be necessary…". This is a **surrogate**: the standard is the duty. It is bounded by contact and closest approach (`p.conflict_horizon`, `p.conflict_centre_clearance`), reusing the yield conventions of LVMC_11_12_070_B.

**Which definition of "stop" applies.** "stop" is ambiguous in the table between two definitions that each state their own scope. Here a stop is *required*, so DEF-NRS-484A-255 ("when required") governs by its own words. `drv.motion.complete_halt` quotes that definition.

**Readings, disclosed here because the validator rejects narrowings on subject and trigger spans:**
- **(a) The protected person.** The person "wholly or partially blind, carrying a cane … or being assisted by a person" is `ru.pedestrian_with_white_cane_or_guide_animal`. That class contract restates these words.
- **(b) The subject's own blindness.** "not wholly or partially blind" is read as the subject *not* being of that class. A blind pedestrian with no cane and no guide is therefore bound. **Reversal signal:** a reviewer rejecting (b). The span then becomes an atom gap for visual impairment, which would block the law.
- **(c) "approaches".** This is the moving subject's centre distance first falling to `p.blind_person_approach_reach`, or the start of contact. The trigger is that *first* reaching, so a subject that halts and then moves on within the reach does not approach again. Without this, o1 and o2 would contradict each other.
- **(d) "with wisdom".** This qualifies the helper, not the protected person. It is a residue of scope none.
- **(e) "before proceeding" (o2).** This refers to o1's stop. It keeps its subject, its object (the same person), its event and its order: a halt after the event, then motion after the halt. It is carried by `drv.motion.complete_halt`, not by composing o1, because the words require the stop itself and not compliance with a rule.

**Reversal signal:** a label that counts a vehicle passing a white-cane pedestrian well outside the reach as an approach. That would change the reach value, not the structure.

## LVMC_11_38_030 — no motorcycles or motor scooters on sidewalks
- **Classes.** "motorcycle" is the admitted aggregate. "motor scooter" has no definition. Large scooters are already motorcycles under the NRS definition, and small ones are mopeds, which that definition excludes. So "motor scooter" maps to `ru.moped`. The stand-up electric scooter is excluded because the code defines it separately and regulates it in chapter 11.40.
- **Duty.** "be ridden" means not `drv.motion.complete_halt`, read as an agency observation. "of the City" reuses `asm.within_city_limits`.
- **Reversal signal:** an LVMC definition of "motor scooter" that includes electric scooters. Then add `ru.electric_scooter`.

## LVMC_11_38_120_B_o1 — lamp equipment (gap)
- **Why a gap.** "shall carry at least one lighted headlamp capable of … and one tail lamp mounted on the rear …" is an equipment duty. `sig.headlamp` and `sig.position_lamp` only say whether a lamp is lit at an observation.
- **Gap filed:** atom `ru.lamp_equipment`. The node will not be coded.
- **Subject reference.** "covered under this Section, as provided in Section 11.38.080" points to a section outside the corpus. It is a residue, so the rule binds the whole vehicle aggregate.
- **Reversal signal:** the ontology admitting lamp equipment, or 11.38.080 entering the corpus. That reference would then become a composition or a law-local aggregate.

## LVMC_11_38_120_B_o2 — lamps burning when in motion in darkness or poor visibility
- **Duty.** The vehicle is in motion (not `complete_halt`), and either `env.darkness` holds or `env.visibility` is below the stated 500 ft. Then `sig.headlamp` must be `low_beam` or `high_beam`, and `sig.position_lamp` must be lit.
- **"The lights required by this Section".** This refers back to s3's headlamp and tail lamp. Their colour and visible range belong to o1's equipment duty. Being lit is this node's duty.
- **Reversal signal:** a reviewer requiring the tail lamp to be told apart from the other position lamps. That would need an atom gap.

## LVMC_11_40_070 — obey the traffic-control devices that apply to vehicles (gap)
- **Why a gap.** The instructions a device gives *vehicles* are stated by the corpus's vehicle rules. A bicycle, electric bicycle or electric scooter is excluded from the vehicle aggregate. `Formula.rule` treats an engaged-less rule as complied with, so composing a vehicle rule for a bicycle would always report compliance.
- **Gap filed:** operator `ruleAsClass`, which reads a rule with its subject's class replaced.
- **Exception.** "unless otherwise directed by a Police Officer" is `dev.human_direction` with role `police_officer`, governing the subject's region. This follows the flagman pattern of LVMC_11_16_030.
- **Reversal signal:** the operator admitting `ruleAsClass`, or deciding that device obedience is to be written per device kind in the rule itself.

## LVMC_11_40_080_o1 — restricted turns for bicycles and scooters
- **Trigger.** A `dev.regulatory_sign` with code `no_right_turn`, `no_left_turn` or `no_u_turn` governs (`dev.governs`) a travel region the rider occupies at some moment while the turn is under way.
- **Obligation.** The rider does not make the turn the sign's code prohibits. Turns are recognised by the three new turn concepts. The left and right turns use a heading band [`turn_min`, `u_turn_min`). The U-turn uses [`u_turn_min`, 360° − `u_turn_min`], so no turn is counted twice and a full loop is not a U-turn. Each turn is recognised when the yaw rate settles.
- **Timing of the trigger and exception.** The sign is read `some_moment`. "dismounts … to make any such turn" is an exception read `throughout`: the person is in the pedestrian aggregate (afoot) at every under-way observation of the turn. This is disclosed here because a narrowing on an exception span is rejected.
- **Reversal signals:**
  - a label that counts a sign governing only the approach lane, before the turn begins. The trigger would then need an event-relative history instead of `some_moment`.
  - a three-point U-turn being recognised as a left turn at its mid pause.

## LVMC_11_40_080_o2 — pedestrian rules after dismounting (gap)
- **Why a gap.** "in which event such person shall then obey the regulations applicable to pedestrians" requires the open set of pedestrian rules. `Formula.rule` composes one named node at a time, and none of the corpus's pedestrian nodes is published as composable yet.
- **Gap filed:** operator `compliesWithClassRules`, which is close to the carried-over G22. Note: this gap also keeps LVMC-11-40-080 blocked as a law, even though o1 is codable.
- **Reversal signal:** the operator deciding that the clause adds no duty beyond the pedestrian rules' own scope. It would then become a scope-none residue.

## LVMC_11_40_120 — use the bicycle path, not the roadway
This is one obligation, not two: "shall use such path and shall not use the roadway" states one choice of place, positively and negatively.
- **Condition.** "usable" is a standard. A path is usable when its width (`st.lane_width`) is at least `p.usable_path_width_min` (AASHTO operating space) and no device closes it: no `dev.regulatory_sign` with code `closed_to_traffic` or `bicycles_prohibited`, and no governing `dev.temporary_traffic_control`.
- **Path and adjacency.** The path is `st.bicycle_lane_or_path`. "adjacent to a roadway" is read through `st.on_way` on a shared `st.highway`. No relation atom separates a path beside the roadway from a bike lane inside it, so both count. This is disclosed here because a narrowing on a condition span is rejected.
- **Obligation.** Travelling along the roadway while off the path is violated. Crossing the roadway (`moving_across_carrier` with the new `p.rider_crossing_motion_cos`, a rider version of the pedestrian tolerance) is not a use of it. A rider on the sidewalk is not judged.
- **Reversal signal:** a reviewer splitting the obligation into two nodes. The second node would then judge a rider who is off the path and on the sidewalk.

## For the operator
- **`env.darkness` boundary.** LVMC_11_38_120_B_o2 reads "from one-half hour after sunset to one-half hour before sunrise" through `env.darkness`. That atom's sunset and sunrise offset is a reading parameter, and the reading must set it to the half hour the law states.
- **LVMC 11.38.080.** This section is cited by LVMC-11-38-120-B but is not in the corpus. Until it is added, both of that law's nodes bind every vehicle.
- **New parameters.** These are proposed with provisional values: `p.blind_person_approach_reach`, `p.immediate_stop_window`, `p.turn_window`, `p.turn_heading_min`, `p.u_turn_heading_min`, `p.turn_yaw_rate_tol`, `p.usable_path_width_min` and `p.rider_crossing_motion_cos`. Earlier-batch parameters are proposed again unchanged: `p.halt_speed_tolerance`, `p.crossing_motion_cos`, `p.conflict_horizon` and `p.conflict_centre_clearance`.
- **Gaps filed.** `ru.lamp_equipment` (atom), `ruleAsClass` (operator) and `compliesWithClassRules` (operator, close to G22). Deciding the two operator gaps together would unblock LVMC-11-40-070 and LVMC-11-40-080.
- **Blindness.** The ontology has no atom for a road user's visual impairment. LVMC_11_30_140_B reads the subject's not being blind as not being of the white-cane class. If that is unacceptable, an atom is needed, and the law blocks without it.

- **(e) "before proceeding" (o2).** This refers to o1's stop. It keeps its subject, its object (the same person), its event and its order: a halt after the event, then motion after the halt. It is carried by `drv.motion.complete_halt`, not by composing o1, because the words require the stop itself and not compliance with a rule.

**Reversal signal:** a label that counts a vehicle passing a white-cane pedestrian well outside the reach as an approach. That would change the reach value, not the structure.

## LVMC_11_38_030 — no motorcycles or motor scooters on sidewalks
- **Classes.** "motorcycle" is the admitted aggregate. "motor scooter" has no definition. Large scooters are already motorcycles under the NRS definition, and small ones are mopeds, which that definition excludes. So "motor scooter" maps to `ru.moped`. The stand-up electric scooter is excluded because the code defines it separately and regulates it in chapter 11.40.
- **Duty.** "be ridden" means not `drv.motion.complete_halt`, read as an agency observation. "of the City" reuses `asm.within_city_limits`.
- **Reversal signal:** an LVMC definition of "motor scooter" that includes electric scooters. Then add `ru.electric_scooter`.

## LVMC_11_38_120_B_o1 — lamp equipment (gap)
- **Why a gap.** "shall carry at least one lighted headlamp capable of … and one tail lamp mounted on the rear …" is an equipment duty. `sig.headlamp` and `sig.position_lamp` only say whether a lamp is lit at an observation.
- **Gap filed:** atom `ru.lamp_equipment`. The node will not be coded.
- **Subject reference.** "covered under this Section, as provided in Section 11.38.080" points to a section outside the corpus. It is a residue, so the rule binds the whole vehicle aggregate.
- **Reversal signal:** the ontology admitting lamp equipment, or 11.38.080 entering the corpus. That reference would then become a composition or a law-local aggregate.

## LVMC_11_38_120_B_o2 — lamps burning when in motion in darkness or poor visibility
- **Duty.** The vehicle is in motion (not `complete_halt`), and either `env.darkness` holds or `env.visibility` is below the stated 500 ft. Then `sig.headlamp` must be `low_beam` or `high_beam`, and `sig.position_lamp` must be lit.
- **"The lights required by this Section".** This refers back to s3's headlamp and tail lamp. Their colour and visible range belong to o1's equipment duty. Being lit is this node's duty.
- **Reversal signal:** a reviewer requiring the tail lamp to be told apart from the other position lamps. That would need an atom gap.

## LVMC_11_40_070 — obey the traffic-control devices that apply to vehicles (gap)
- **Why a gap.** The instructions a device gives *vehicles* are stated by the corpus's vehicle rules. A bicycle, electric bicycle or electric scooter is excluded from the vehicle aggregate. `Formula.rule` treats an engaged-less rule as complied with, so composing a vehicle rule for a bicycle would always report compliance.
- **Gap filed:** operator `ruleAsClass`, which reads a rule with its subject's class replaced.
- **Exception.** "unless otherwise directed by a Police Officer" is `dev.human_direction` with role `police_officer`, governing the subject's region. This follows the flagman pattern of LVMC_11_16_030.
- **Reversal signal:** the operator admitting `ruleAsClass`, or deciding that device obedience is to be written per device kind in the rule itself.

## LVMC_11_40_080_o1 — restricted turns for bicycles and scooters
- **Trigger.** A `dev.regulatory_sign` with code `no_right_turn`, `no_left_turn` or `no_u_turn` governs (`dev.governs`) a travel region the rider occupies at some moment while the turn is under way.
- **Obligation.** The rider does not make the turn the sign's code prohibits. Turns are recognised by the three new turn concepts. The left and right turns use a heading band [`turn_min`, `u_turn_min`). The U-turn uses [`u_turn_min`, 360° − `u_turn_min`], so no turn is counted twice and a full loop is not a U-turn. Each turn is recognised when the yaw rate settles.
- **Timing of the trigger and exception.** The sign is read `some_moment`. "dismounts … to make any such turn" is an exception read `throughout`: the person is in the pedestrian aggregate (afoot) at every under-way observation of the turn. This is disclosed here because a narrowing on an exception span is rejected.
- **Reversal signals:**
  - a label that counts a sign governing only the approach lane, before the turn begins. The trigger would then need an event-relative history instead of `some_moment`.
  - a three-point U-turn being recognised as a left turn at its mid pause.

## LVMC_11_40_080_o2 — pedestrian rules after dismounting (gap)
- **Why a gap.** "in which event such person shall then obey the regulations applicable to pedestrians" requires the open set of pedestrian rules. `Formula.rule` composes one named node at a time, and none of the corpus's pedestrian nodes is published as composable yet.
- **Gap filed:** operator `compliesWithClassRules`, which is close to the carried-over G22. Note: this gap also keeps LVMC-11-40-080 blocked as a law, even though o1 is codable.
- **Reversal signal:** the operator deciding that the clause adds no duty beyond the pedestrian rules' own scope. It would then become a scope-none residue.

## LVMC_11_40_120 — use the bicycle path, not the roadway
This is one obligation, not two: "shall use such path and shall not use the roadway" states one choice of place, positively and negatively.
- **Condition.** "usable" is a standard. A path is usable when its width (`st.lane_width`) is at least `p.usable_path_width_min` (AASHTO operating space) and no device closes it: no `dev.regulatory_sign` with code `closed_to_traffic` or `bicycles_prohibited`, and no governing `dev.temporary_traffic_control`.
- **Path and adjacency.** The path is `st.bicycle_lane_or_path`. "adjacent to a roadway" is read through `st.on_way` on a shared `st.highway`. No relation atom separates a path beside the roadway from a bike lane inside it, so both count. This is disclosed here because a narrowing on a condition span is rejected.
- **Obligation.** Travelling along the roadway while off the path is violated. Crossing the roadway (`moving_across_carrier` with the new `p.rider_crossing_motion_cos`, a rider version of the pedestrian tolerance) is not a use of it. A rider on the sidewalk is not judged.
- **Reversal signal:** a reviewer splitting the obligation into two nodes. The second node would then judge a rider who is off the path and on the sidewalk.

## For the operator
- **`env.darkness` boundary.** LVMC_11_38_120_B_o2 reads "from one-half hour after sunset to one-half hour before sunrise" through `env.darkness`. That atom's sunset and sunrise offset is a reading parameter, and the reading must set it to the half hour the law states.
- **LVMC 11.38.080.** This section is cited by LVMC-11-38-120-B but is not in the corpus. Until it is added, both of that law's nodes bind every vehicle.
- **New parameters.** These are proposed with provisional values: `p.blind_person_approach_reach`, `p.immediate_stop_window`, `p.turn_window`, `p.turn_heading_min`, `p.u_turn_heading_min`, `p.turn_yaw_rate_tol`, `p.usable_path_width_min` and `p.rider_crossing_motion_cos`. Earlier-batch parameters are proposed again unchanged: `p.halt_speed_tolerance`, `p.crossing_motion_cos`, `p.conflict_horizon` and `p.conflict_centre_clearance`.
- **Gaps filed.** `ru.lamp_equipment` (atom), `ruleAsClass` (operator) and `compliesWithClassRules` (operator, close to G22). Deciding the two operator gaps together would unblock LVMC-11-40-070 and LVMC-11-40-080.
- **Blindness.** The ontology has no atom for a road user's visual impairment. LVMC_11_30_140_B reads the subject's not being blind as not being of the white-cane class. If that is unacceptable, an atom is needed, and the law blocks without it.

content.text:
I've planned all eight laws as 11 nodes plus 3 new turn concepts, and the validator accepts every node and concept. Three of the nodes carry gaps, so the coder won't write those, and three laws stay blocked: LVMC-11-38-120-B, LVMC-11-40-070 and LVMC-11-40-080.

| Node | What it checks | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `LVMC_11_30_070_B` | A pedestrian crossing a roadway must be in a crosswalk (marked or unmarked) | Business district is a new assumption, `asm.business_district`. The existing one also covers residence districts, so I didn't reuse it. |
| `LVMC_11_30_090` | A pedestrian may not walk along a roadway when a sidewalk lies on the same highway | Uses the same angle as the crossing rule to tell "along" from "across". |
| `LVMC_11_30_140_B_o1` | A sighted pedestrian or a vehicle that comes near or into contact with a white-cane pedestrian must stop within a short time | "Immediately" is set by a time window; "comes near" by a distance. |
| `LVMC_11_30_140_B_o2` | After that stop, the subject must not touch or come close to the person while moving off | Surrogate: the law states the duty only as a judgement standard, so this is an approximation by contact and near-miss checks. |
| `LVMC_11_38_030` | No motorcycle or "motor scooter" moving on a sidewalk within city limits | "Motor scooter" is mapped to moped. |
| `LVMC_11_38_120_B_o1` | Lamp equipment | **Gap:** the ontology has nothing for what lamps a vehicle carries (proposed atom `ru.lamp_equipment`). |
| `LVMC_11_38_120_B_o2` | Headlamp and tail lamps lit when moving in darkness or visibility under 500 ft | |
| `LVMC_11_40_070` | Bicycles and scooters obey traffic-control devices | **Gap:** composing the vehicle rules for a bicycle always reports compliance, because a bicycle isn't a vehicle. I proposed operator `ruleAsClass`. |
| `LVMC_11_40_080_o1` | No right, left or U-turn where a sign prohibits it, unless the rider is on foot for the whole turn | Uses the 3 new turn concepts. |
| `LVMC_11_40_080_o2` | Obey pedestrian rules after dismounting | **Gap:** this needs the whole open set of pedestrian rules (proposed operator `compliesWithClassRules`). It also keeps o1's law blocked even though o1 can be coded. |
| `LVMC_11_40_120` | Bicycles and scooters must use an adjacent usable path rather than ride along the roadway | One node, not two. A path is "usable" when wide enough and not closed by a sign. |

Choices worth reviewing:
- **Blindness (`LVMC_11_30_140_B`):** "not wholly or partially blind" is read as the pedestrian not carrying a white cane or being led. A blind pedestrian without a cane is therefore bound by the rule. If a reviewer rejects that, the span becomes a gap and the law blocks.
- **Readings the validator wouldn't take as recorded narrowings:** It rejects readings recorded on the spans that decide when a rule applies. I removed those entries and wrote the readings up in `PLAN.md` instead:
  - the blindness reading above;
  - the "approaches" distance;
  - "dismounts" meaning on foot for the whole turn;
  - "adjacent" meaning lying on the same highway.
- **Section 11.38.080:** `LVMC-11-38-120-B` cites this section, but it isn't in the corpus. Until it is, both of that law's nodes apply to every vehicle.

For you:
- The half-hour after sunset and before sunrise in `LVMC_11_38_120_B_o2` depends on the reading setting the darkness atom's offset to exactly half an hour.
- I proposed eight new parameters with provisional values, and re-proposed four from earlier batches unchanged.
- Deciding the two operator gaps together would unblock `LVMC-11-40-070` and `LVMC-11-40-080`.

Files are in `iter-001/plan/batch-03`:
- blueprint.jsonl
- aggregates.jsonl (empty: no law-local aggregates)
- PLAN.md
